kbuild.driver_prompt: Goldfish address space support in Rust
driver_help: Build the Rust goldfish address space driver.

defconfig_test.h.reason: This is Android-side build/test scaffolding and does not belong in the upstream landing plan.
defconfig_test.h.rust_strategy: Omit from the upstream Rust driver and rely on in-tree configuration/build plumbing instead.

goldfish/goldfish_address_space.h.reason: This header carries the userspace-visible ioctl and shared layout contract, so the upstream plan needs an explicit UAPI landing decision instead of treating it as an opaque private include.
goldfish/goldfish_address_space.h.rust_strategy: Land a typed UAPI/header surface first; route the Rust driver through translated constants and request layouts instead of direct bindgen-visible private headers.

translation.goal: Drive `drivers/platform/goldfish/goldfish_address_space.rs` to an artifact-constrained PCI + miscdevice implementation that closes `open/release/ioctl/mmap` and carries the driver through runtime differential against the C baseline while keeping equivalence claims limited to the currently covered ABI subset.
translation.abstraction_goal: Stage the external-source `goldfish_address_space` target through explicit Rust abstractions for PCI, miscdevice, page-backed ping state, shared BAR ownership, user copy, and VMA mapping so the driver can close `open/release/ioctl/mmap` without driver-side unsafe.

mvp_scope.note: This round now claims PCI probe/remove plus miscdevice userspace API closure together with expanded minimal-guest differential over the current ABI subset. Broader host protocol coverage remains a later oracle.

body_plan: Use the existing PCI abstraction to bind the device and create the per-device Rust owner.
Register the miscdevice from probe and keep the registration inside the driver-owned Rust state.
Let owned Rust state drop in a way that unregisters the miscdevice and tears down probe state without raw remove code in the driver.
Use typed miscdevice registration data to hand per-device runtime into `open` without raw `container_of` logic in driver code.
Allocate a page-backed ping buffer and create typed per-file state that owns the host handle and mapping bookkeeping.
Keep release coupled to the miscdevice abstraction and drive teardown from owned Rust state rather than raw file-private casts.
Destroy the host handle and reclaim guest-owned blocks from typed per-file state.
Decode user requests through `UserSlice` plus explicit byte-encoded ioctl wrappers so driver code stays zero-unsafe and zero-bindings.
Route allocate/deallocate/ping/claim flows through typed Rust state and abstraction-owned user copy helpers.
Reuse the typed ioctl path for compat handling because the current UAPI payloads stay width-stable across compat mode.
Authorize `mmap` through the explicit `SharedMemoryBar` owner plus `VmaNew::iomap_memory` wrapper rather than raw `remap_pfn_range` in driver code.
Gate the mapping by checking requested ranges against typed owned/shared block tracking before exposing the BAR to userspace.

device_table: Translate the goldfish PCI device id table through `kernel::pci_device_table!` before code generation.

private_state.layout: PCI-bound Rust owner created from probe

fields.name: misc
fields.role: Own the miscdevice registration so remove/drop can tear it down soundly.

private_state.note: Per-device runtime now owns the control/shared BAR abstractions, while per-file `Arc<FileState>` owns the ping page, host handle, and mapping bookkeeping.

commands.success_witness: The command completes only if the status register reports success, after which the block offset and size may be read back.
commands.failure_witness: A non-zero status register value is translated into the returned error.

c_evidence.note: The external C driver calls `as_run_command(..., AS_COMMAND_ALLOCATE_BLOCK)` and then reads back offset/size.

commands.success_witness: The command completes only if the status register reports success.
commands.failure_witness: A non-zero status register value is translated into the returned error.

c_evidence.note: The external C driver returns `as_run_command(..., AS_COMMAND_DEALLOCATE_BLOCK)` directly.

commands.success_witness: Completion is validated by reading back a non-invalid handle from the HANDLE register.
commands.failure_witness: If the readback handle is `GOLDFISH_AS_INVALID_HANDLE`, the helper returns `EINVAL`.

c_evidence.note: The external C driver issues `AS_COMMAND_GEN_HANDLE` and validates the HANDLE readback instead of gating on STATUS.

commands.success_witness: Completion is validated by reading back the echoed ping-info physical address from the device registers.
commands.failure_witness: If the echoed physical address differs from the programmed address, the helper returns `EINVAL`.

c_evidence.note: The external C driver issues `AS_COMMAND_TELL_PING_INFO_ADDR` and validates the echoed physical address readback.

commands.success_witness: The command is issued after programming the handle register; teardown stays best-effort on the release path.
commands.failure_witness: No new STATUS/readback gate may be introduced on the release path.

c_evidence.note: The external C driver issues `AS_COMMAND_DESTROY_HANDLE` on release and does not gate teardown on STATUS or readback.
